chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from one of our companions, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

You should say upon the Aqeeqa: [a similar supplication was mentioned], and he added in it: 'O Allah, its flesh for his flesh, and its blood for his blood, and its bone for his bone, and its hair for his hair, and its skin for his skin. O Allah, make it a shield for so-and-so, son of so-and-so.'

key_terms.اللَّهُمَّ: O Allah: The vocative form of God used to initiate supplication.
key_terms.عَقِيقَة: Aqeeqa: The ritual slaughter of an animal in gratitude for the birth of a child.
key_terms.فُلَانِ بْنِ فُلَانٍ: So-and-so, son of so-and-so: A placeholder for the specific name of the child and their father.
key_terms.لَحْمُهَا: Its flesh: Referring to the meat of the sacrificed animal.
key_terms.وِقَاءً: A shield/protection: Referring to the protective merit of the sacrifice for the child.

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite when performing the Aqeeqa sacrifice for a newborn?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the ritual supplication for Aqeeqa, emphasizing the theological concept of vicarious substitution where the animal's physical attributes serve as a protective shield (wiqaa') for the newborn. In Shia tradition, this practice is viewed not merely as cultural but as a Sunnah of the Imams, linking the child's spiritual protection to the sacrificial offering. The specific invocation highlights the intimate connection between the child and the sacrifice, reinforcing the belief in divine safeguarding through ritual acts.
